Guillermo's own take for Mon, Nov 9 (his read, quote it as his, not yours): Outflow is building. Pam Rocks read N 24 gusting 29 at 7am, up from 22 at 5am and a touch ahead of the page's 23. Pemberton is still 2 hPa above Vancouver, and Environment Canada's 4am update keeps the strong wind warning for Howe Sound, outflow 20 to 25 easing near noon.

My pick is Porteau now until about 11am, NNE 20 to 22 with waves. The tide topped out at 15.1ft at 7:16am and ebbs all morning. Check before driving: Pam Rocks 22 or more on the 8am reading, go; under 20, stay home.

EC marine forecast, Howe Sound (issued 05:40 PM PCT 09 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Tuesday. Strong wind warning in effect. Wind northerly outflow 20 to 30 knots diminishing to southerly inflow 15 this evening then becoming northerly outflow 10 to 20 late overnight. Wind becoming northerly outflow 15 to 25 Tuesday morning.

EC marine forecast, Strait of Georgia (south of Nanaimo) (issued 05:40 PM PCT 09 November 2026), WARNING IN EFFECT: Tonight and Tuesday. Gale warning in effect. Wind east 15 to 20 knots veering to southeast 20 to 25 early this evening then to southwest 15 to 20 late this evening. Wind backing to southeast 15 to 25 after midnight then becoming southeast 20 to 30 Tuesday afternoon except southeast 35 south of Tsawwassen Tuesday evening.
